summary: The theoretical review is substantially accurate and its verdict is correct: REVISION REQUIRED, one bounded response_to_review, frozen specification retained. Independent re-execution reproduces the five test failures, the stale Gate 2 review, the denominator collisions, our own five-versus-six and commit-count contradictions, and both kernel-gate weaknesses. Four claims need correction, one requested action (a real assistive-technology transcript) cannot be produced by the agent team, and round 3 of 3 means this response must be self-sufficient.
intended_user_outcome: Unchanged and correctly restated by the theory pole: a first-time visitor discovers art, admires works, forms and recovers a local Taste Passport, and understands how their actions affect it — and can do all of that with a keyboard, with a screen reader, at 320 to 1440 pixels, in both themes, at 200 percent zoom, with every rendered image's rights basis honestly recorded rather than claimed as cleared. The review does not redefine that outcome, does not reopen the information architecture, the artist-first hierarchy, or any of the 29 frozen criteria, and explicitly refuses the deferred features. What it demands is that the evidence for the outcome be true, current, reproducible, and bound to one commit.
essential_principles: RA1 ESSENTIAL — close and independently remeasure V32-1..V32-7. AC19 is frozen; six measured majors are open; V32-7 renders at 1.00-1.04 contrast on the mobile search path, which is an AC21 defect as well. Feasible with the existing Chrome measurement harness.

The named selectors are measurable. Focus-RING contrast (WCAG 1.4.11) is not: browser-evidence-enumeration.md section 6.4 records it as structurally unmeasurable by a glyph differential, and it sits in NOT TESTED item 3. Underlying principle is satisfied by a source-derived two-colour bound declared as a bound, plus captured evidence — never by inference from a neighbouring selector, which is the exact error A13 was called to correct.

RA4 ESSENTIAL — regenerate candidate asset and rights inventories at final HEAD and disposition every delta. AC10, AC11 and AC12 are frozen. constraints_or_principles_to_defend: OD-5 IS OURS AND WE BROKE IT. The owner decided on 2026-07-23: 'the register records asserted basis, attribution, and residual uncertainty; any actual clearance claim requires qualified review; unresolved items are labeled unresolved, never cleared.' AC12 says the same. The build evidence report then wrote 'three replaced with verified-PD files' and 'Both photographer-copyright frescoes replaced with genuinely PD images'. Those are assertions of legal status. The theory pole is right, and the correct posture is not to argue the point but to concede it in the response.

The precise shape of the breach matters and should be stated, because it is a lesson rather than an excuse: the machine-checked surface complies and the human-facing prose does not. tests/test_rights_tooling.py TestRegisterLanguage enforces OD-5 on the register ('the register may say asserted; it may never say cleared') and it passes. Nothing tested the narrative report. A rule enforced only where a test looks is not enforced.

Bounded language is cheap and principled, so there is no reason to negotiate it. 'Commons metadata asserts public domain, licence X, retrieved 2026-07-DD; exact-work match confirmed against the file page; no independent legal determination made' costs nothing and is more useful evidence than 'verified-PD'.

Existential claims must be bounded to the audit. 'No suitable Kahlo image is available' is not a finding this audit can support; 'this audit's Commons searches, listed here, did not locate a candidate meeting the exact-work test' is.

Reviewer independence is non-negotiable and constrains how we staff this response. Van Eyck must re-review at final HEAD and must produce none of the fixes; the AC19 remeasurement must again be run by a non-implementer under Van Eyck's A13 ruling, since that is precisely the arrangement that found the six majors two implementer-run censuses had missed.

Enumeration over sampling, and never inference from a neighbouring selector. This build has now been wrong three times by sampling and once by asserting clearance from the stylesheet. RA2's 'do not infer clearance from neighbouring selectors' is our own hard-won rule quoted back at us, and it should be honoured rather than defended against.
The frozen specification stays frozen. The theory pole agrees. Supplementary evidence at 900 and 1024 pixels is welcome; adding acceptance criteria at round 3 of 3 is not, in either direction.

No merge, no deployment, no human_review_ready while Gate 2 is uncertified. AC29 and CLAUDE.md Gate 2. This is not conceded under pressure; it was already our position and the report already refused to claim certification.

critical_issues: ROUND BUDGET — this response is the last cross-pole exchange and must be self-sufficient. state.json has round 3 and max_rounds 3. engine.py line 361 expects a response_to_review at state['round'] = 3, so ours is admissible. engine.py line 355 expects any further review at state['round'] + 1 = 4, and lines 139-140 raise GateError('Deliberation round budget exhausted') above max_rounds. Consequence: there is no round in which theory can accept our answers, so the response cannot say 'we will address X next round', cannot leave a question open for their adjudication, and cannot assume they will validate our remeasurement. Every one of the thirteen actions must be either closed, or closed-with-a-recorded-residual-risk that the OWNER (not theory) can act on. If we conclude we need another theory round, that is an owner decision to raise max_rounds, and it must be raised at the start of the work rather than discovered at the end of it.

OUR OWN OUTGOING CONTROL FAILED, TWICE OVER, AND MY AUDIT IS PART OF THE FAILURE. Verified: messages/006-implementation_report.json says 'SIX open major findings' in summary and 'AC19 has six open major findings' in the proposal, but its rationale says 'five measured findings remain' and its routing paragraph says 'that is the right place for these five'. Separately, summary and proposal both say '75 commits' — true of effa805..5c684ae (75), false of the SHA actually routed, 55fb166 (76), and now doubly false at HEAD c5cf859 (77). My build_review audit returned the report and D-018 repaired the specific instances I named; neither swept the document for the same quantity elsewhere, and neither recomputed the count against the routed SHA. The lesson for the response: when a quantity changes, re-derive it at EVERY occurrence, and compute counts against the exact commit being transmitted, because HEAD advances every time the kernel routes a message.

TESTS: 'make the suite pass' and 'do not mask unexplained drift' are in tension here and the response must say so explicitly or it will look like tuning. Three of the five failures are caused by a documented, benign content addition (D-016 / ef8b2b3): museum_photos_rendered 103->104 is one added Guggenheim photograph; gallery_rendered and prerender_metadata_refs carry the corresponding content-lane records. The correct remedy is to extend the existing CORRECTIONS ledger in tests/test_rights_tooling.py with a dated, per-URL justification for each addition — which is exactly what that ledger exists for ('an undocumented image change cannot slip through as expected drift') — and to re-freeze the headline counts with the same justification. Changing 797 to 798 with no ledger entry would be the masking they warn against; refusing to change it at all would fail a test for a legitimate content addition.

A SIXTH FAILURE IS HIDING BEHIND THE FIRST. tests/test_rights_tooling.py:276 asserts copyright_refs == 60; the current value is 66. It is not among the five failures only because line 271 (total_unique 798 != 797) aborts the same test method before reaching it. Whoever fixes line 271 will surface line 276 immediately. The response should fix both together and say that it did, or the next run will look like a regression.

KERNEL GATE DEFECT 1 — the build gate binds to a branch, never to a SHA. pigment_coordinator/gates.py check_build_gate(repo_root, branch, baseline) resolves branch^{commit} at call time and verifies ancestry, commit count and production-file touch; it never records the SHA, and never checks that the SHA is the one the report describes. Theory's claim reproduces exactly. The response should bind the final report, validator output, test output, screenshots and Quality Review to one named SHA in the artifacts themselves, since the gate will not do it for us.

KERNEL GATE DEFECT 2 — the quality gate cannot tell an operative verdict from an archived one. check_quality_gate runs re.search for 'GATE 2: CERTIFIED', 'OPEN CRITICAL: 0' and 'OPEN MAJOR: 0' case-insensitively over the whole of quality-review.md, which is append-only and currently contains three revisions' verdict blocks. Today it happens to block, because no revision has ever said CERTIFIED. The moment one does, every later BLOCKED revision becomes invisible to the gate. This is a genuine defect in the arbiter and it is more serious than the D-017 disclosure itself.

AC15 CANNOT BE SATISFIED BY THIS TEAM. The criterion is frozen with the words 'tested assistive-technology setup'. No agent can drive VoiceOver and honestly transcribe what it announced. Gate 2 requires all 29 criteria to pass, so as things stand Gate 2 cannot certify however well the other twelve actions go. This must be settled at the START of the response work, not at the end, because round 3 of 3 offers no recovery.

AC19's PERIMETER IS STILL NOT CLOSED, AND THE RESPONSE MUST NOT PRETEND OTHERWISE. evidence/browser-evidence-enumeration.md declines to claim completeness and lists 17 NOT TESTED classes, including .map-dot .md-name (flagged as the likeliest place a further SVG finding hides, same --muted class as V32-1), focus-ring contrast everywhere but .hero, 553 fully-occluded rows, single-draw canvas confirmation, and the crashed pseudo-element perimeter scan whose site list came from reading the CSS rather than the DOM. Seurat (Data and Copyright Steward) — REQUIRED, not optional this time. Owns the denominator glossary, the AC11 no-asset disposition for beginning-noland, the reconciliation of every ef8b2b3 content-lane delta, and the OD-5 language sweep replacing verified-PD / genuinely PD / status-is-true / unavailable-image across the report, the register and the decision record.

Van Eyck (Quality and Accessibility Reviewer) — fresh Quality Review at final HEAD across all 29 criteria, ending with an unambiguous operative verdict bound to that SHA. INDEPENDENCE IS BINDING: he produces none of the fixes, does not operate the remeasurement, and does not draft the report he certifies. He should also be asked to rule on how AC15 is dispositioned if no assistive-technology session happens.
Matisse (Visual Design Director) — N-8 only, against the final light and dark surfaces, after Vermeer's recapture. Not before.

Mondrian (UX and Interaction Architect) — narrow: V32-7 was referred to her as N-31-2 and the mobile nav overpainting the open search panel is a layout decision, not a colour token. Also the F-2 masked focus ring.

Rubens (Synthesis Lead) — consolidates the response_to_review, and personally owns the two things the last report got wrong: sweeping every changed quantity through every occurrence, and binding every artifact to one named SHA.

NOT recommended: Caravaggio (nothing here needs an assumption challenge — we are conceding, not disputing) and Van Gogh (no editorial-voice work in scope). Do not convene the full team; nine of thirteen actions are evidence work, not deliberation.
recommended_next_state: revision — hold at revision and produce ONE response_to_review at round 3, which engine.py accepts (line 361, expected round = state.round = 3) and which is the LAST admissible cross-pole exchange, since any further review would be round 4 and raise GateError above max_rounds 3

human_escalation.reason_category: essential information that cannot responsibly be inferred, and that neither pole can produce
human_escalation.decision_required: AC15 is frozen with the words 'exposes one meaningful page identity to the tested assistive-technology setup'. No agent can operate VoiceOver and honestly report what it announced, and fabricating a transcript is absolutely forbidden. VoiceOver and Safari are both installed on this machine, so a person can do it. Arda should choose one of: (a) run, or authorise someone to run, one scripted VoiceOver plus Safari session over route identity, search, Passport import conflicts, onboarding recovery, state controls and the influence-graph bypass, with the team supplying the script and recording the observations; or (b) accept AC15 as unmet with an explicit residual-risk disposition, which keeps Gate 2 uncertified and the product short of human_review_ready; or (c) extend max_rounds so the question can be carried into a further exchange. A separate and later decision, flagged now but not needed yet: whether the two Coordinator-kernel commits on this branch (d2b935d/D-012 and 5fdf1aa/D-017) are excluded from, or separately proposed for, any eventual user-approved merge — pigment_coordinator/ is tracked in this same tree, so a branch merge carries them.
human_escalation.why_the_teams_cannot_resolve_it: The evidence AC15 requires is a human observation of assistive-technology output. The Claude pole cannot generate it without fabricating it; the theory pole cannot generate it at all and has correctly refused to accept DOM inspection as a substitute; and the Coordinator cannot waive a frozen criterion. It is time-critical rather than merely open, because round 3 of 3 leaves no exchange in which to discover the answer later.

confidence.basis: Every load-bearing claim was independently re-executed against this working tree at HEAD c5cf859 rather than taken from either pole's account: the 41-test suite with its five failures and their exact assertions; the JXA validator's full count line; asset_inventory.build() counts and a surface-by-surface membership diff against the effa805 freeze; three commit counts against three different SHAs; the literal text of the five-versus-six contradiction in the routed report; the source of check_build_gate and check_quality_gate; the round arithmetic in engine.py; the presence of VoiceOver, Safari and Chrome and the absence of Firefox; and the beginning-noland record in js/catalog-4.js. Lower confidence attaches only to the estimate that closing V32-1..V32-7 will not open a further finding — the enumeration itself declines to claim a closed perimeter, and this build has been surprised on that point four times.

rationale: The theory pole has done the job the protocol asks of it. Their verdict is right, their scope discipline is honest, and eleven of their twelve disputed points reproduce under independent re-execution — including two defects in the Coordinator's own gates that are more serious than the disclosure that led them there. The four corrections I owe them are refinements, not rebuttals: the 76-versus-75 Tier 1 gap is a correct remedy resting on a wrong diagnosis, because the tooling's 75 counts Tier 1 records that have an asset and the assertion encoding it currently passes; the stale copyright_refs expectation is latent rather than live; and the denominator families they call mixed are dated, surface-specific quantities with one documented cause, D-016's content-lane commit ef8b2b3. None of that changes what we must do. The uncomfortable finding is ours. My own build_review audit returned the implementation report and caught the omitted V32-7, D-018 repaired what I named, and both of us then let the same document go out saying six in two places and five in two others, with a commit count computed against the last build commit rather than the SHA being transmitted. The theory pole caught it. An outgoing control that fixes only the instances it was pointed at is not a control, and the response should say so plainly rather than filing it as an erratum. Two things shape the response more than any individual action. First, the round budget: at round 3 of 3 our response_to_review is admissible but no further theory review is, so the response must be self-sufficient — nothing deferred to a next round, nothing left for theory to adjudicate, every open item closed or converted into a residual risk the OWNER can act on. Second, AC15: it is frozen to require a tested assistive-technology setup, we have never met it, and we cannot meet it, because no agent can operate VoiceOver and honestly report what it said. VoiceOver and Safari are on this machine, so a person can. That has to be settled before the work starts, not discovered at the end of it. On the language objection they are simply right, and we should concede it without negotiation: OD-5 bound us on 2026-07-23 to record asserted basis and residual uncertainty and never clearance, and the report then wrote verified-PD and genuinely PD. The instructive detail is that the machine-checked surface complied — TestRegisterLanguage enforces exactly this on the register and passes — while the human-facing prose did not. A rule enforced only where a test looks is not enforced. On D-017 governance: I cannot be the independent party, because I am this pole's own analyst and I was the one who caught it, so a disposition I authored would be the same conflict of interest one level up. It belongs to the Coordinator Kernel as the neutral party, on the record and presented to Arda before any merge, and it should cover both kernel commits rather than the one theory noticed, name the two gate defects, and state plainly whether the kernel change is excluded from the product merge set or proposed separately.

owner_report.title: Synthesis Liaison Report — incoming theoretical review, PIG-001 round 3
owner_report.markdown:
## Current Position

The theory team reviewed the built product and sent it back for one round of corrections. They kept the plan and the 29 acceptance criteria unchanged, and they did not ask for anything new to be designed. They asked for the work to be finished and the evidence to be made true and current.

I checked their claims against the repository myself rather than taking them on trust. Almost all of them hold up.

## Feasibility

Twelve of their thirteen requests are ordinary, achievable work: fix six known contrast failures, fix two responsive layout defects, regenerate the image inventory, publish one table explaining what every count means, correct the rights wording, make the test suite pass, retake the screenshots last, and get a fresh independent quality review.

One request cannot be done by the team at all. One frozen criterion requires that the site be tested with a real screen reader. No AI agent can operate a screen reader and honestly report what it announced, and inventing that record is out of the question. VoiceOver and Safari are both installed on this Mac, so a person can do it in one sitting. This needs your decision — see Attention Required.

## Adaptations Made

I recommend accepting the review essentially in full rather than contesting it, because the checks came back on their side. I also recommend that we volunteer more than they asked for on one point: they noticed one change we made to the neutral coordinator's own code, and there are actually two.

## Product Intent

Preserved. Nothing in this review changes what Pigment is or who it is for. They explicitly declined to reopen the artist-first hierarchy and declined to add any of the deferred features.

## Evidence

Strongest verified support: the site's data validator passes cleanly, both Taste Passport blockers are genuinely fixed, and the rights work found and corrected real errors.

The important gaps: five of forty-one tests fail; six measured contrast failures remain open, one of which makes a label on the mobile search panel effectively invisible; the last independent quality review is out of date; and nothing has been tested with a screen reader or in any browser other than Chrome.

## Remaining Problems

Three things I want on the record rather than smoothed over.

First, our own report went out contradicting itself — it said six open failures in two places and five in two others, and its commit count described a different commit than the one we sent. My audit is supposed to catch exactly that. It caught part of it and missed the rest, and the theory team found what we missed. That is a real weakness in our outgoing checks, not a typo.

Second, we broke one of your own rules. You decided on 23 July that we would record what image licences *assert*, plus the remaining uncertainty, and never claim anything was legally cleared. Our report then described images as "verified public domain" and "genuinely public domain". Those are legal claims we are not entitled to make. The theory team is right and we should simply concede it. Notably, the part of the system that has an automated check for this rule complied; only the human-written prose broke it.

Third, two weaknesses in the coordinator's own safety gates: it verifies a build against a *branch* rather than a specific commit, and it checks the quality review by searching the whole file for approval text — and that file keeps its old superseded reviews. Once any review says approved, later ones saying blocked would go unnoticed. Both are worth fixing.

## Synthesis Assessment

Quality is not yet supported and the product is correctly still short of your review. The corrections are bounded and well understood. The one genuine obstacle is the screen-reader evidence.

## What Happens Next

I have recommended the Coordinator route this to the Claude team to produce one correction response, with six specialists involved and the quality reviewer kept independent of the fixes he will then assess. This is the third and final round of exchange the process allows, so the response has to stand on its own — there is no further round in which the theory team could accept our answers.

## Attention Required

Owner decision may be required: whether you will run (or ask someone to run) a single screen-reader session — VoiceOver with Safari, roughly half an hour, following a script we would prepare — covering page identity on navigation, search, Passport import, onboarding recovery, and the influence graph. The reason is that one of the frozen criteria requires real assistive-technology testing, no agent can produce that evidence honestly, and without it the quality gate cannot pass however well the rest of the work goes. The alternatives are to accept that criterion as unmet with the risk written down, or to allow the teams an extra round of exchange. This is time-critical only because we are in the final permitted round, so it is better settled before the correction work starts than after.
